questions.question: Which aspect best defines a controlled ablation study in large-model experimentation?
questions.choice_A: Systematically removing or altering one component at a time while holding all other factors constant to isolate causal contributions
questions.choice_B: Training multiple models with random hyperparameters and selecting the best-performing variant
questions.choice_C: Benchmarking only on a single dataset to reduce confounding variables
questions.choice_D: Comparing results across unrelated papers without re-running baselines

questions.question: When comparing two model variants on the same test set across multiple random seeds, which statistical test is most appropriate for detecting a mean performance difference under approximate normality and equal-variance assumptions?
questions.choice_A: Unpaired t-test
questions.choice_B: Paired t-test
questions.choice_C: Chi-squared test
questions.choice_D: ANOVA with Tukey HSD

questions.question: A hyperparameter search is performed on a small model due to compute limits. Which practice best supports generalization of the chosen hyperparameters to a larger model?
questions.choice_A: Directly copying the exact learning rate without scaling or validation
questions.choice_B: Maximizing validation accuracy on the small model and assuming linear transfer
questions.choice_C: Selecting hyperparameters guided by scale-aware heuristics (e.g., batch size and LR scaling laws) and validating on a held-out mid-scale model
questions.choice_D: Ignoring optimization dynamics and reusing default settings from prior work

questions.question: Which of the following is the clearest indicator of robust runtime measurement for training throughput?
questions.choice_A: Reporting the fastest observed iteration without context
questions.choice_B: Measuring early iterations before caches and kernels are warmed up
questions.choice_C: Reporting average tokens/sec over a single long run without variance
questions.choice_D: Using multiple runs with warm-up discarded, synchronized timers, and reporting mean ± standard deviation with hardware details

questions.question: In the context of multiple hypothesis testing across many benchmarks, what is the main risk of reporting raw p-values without correction?
questions.choice_A: Inflated family-wise Type I error leading to spurious significance findings
questions.choice_B: Reduction in statistical power for true effects
questions.choice_C: Inability to compute confidence intervals
questions.choice_D: Overestimation of effect size magnitude due to small sample size

questions.question: Which approach is most appropriate for constructing confidence intervals for a non-normal metric like median accuracy across seeds?
questions.choice_A: Parametric CI using the normal approximation
questions.choice_B: Bootstrap percentile intervals with sufficient resamples and seed-stratified sampling
questions.choice_C: Wald interval derived from a logistic model
questions.choice_D: Assuming the CI width is negligible for medians

questions.question: Which source of nondeterminism is most likely to affect reproducibility across GPU trainings even with fixed random seeds?
questions.choice_A: Using a fixed batch size
questions.choice_B: Saving checkpoints with deterministic filenames
questions.choice_C: Non-deterministic CUDA kernels and fused operations that reorder floating-point arithmetic
questions.choice_D: Logging to a local file instead of the cloud

questions.question: What constitutes a fair and comparable hyperparameter tuning protocol for baselines versus a new method?
questions.choice_A: Tuning the new method exhaustively and using default hyperparameters for baselines
questions.choice_B: Using a different validation set for each method to maximize performance
questions.choice_C: Stopping baseline training early to save compute
questions.choice_D: Applying symmetric budgets, identical search spaces where applicable, and the same validation criteria for selection

questions.question: When reporting memory usage for training a large model with activation checkpointing and mixed precision, which is the most informative metric?
questions.choice_A: Peak device memory measured with clear methodology, including precision mode, batch size, gradient accumulation steps, and activation checkpointing settings
questions.choice_B: Minimum memory observed during a single iteration
questions.choice_C: CPU memory only, since GPU memory is hardware-dependent
questions.choice_D: An anecdotal estimate based on similar models

questions.question: Which practice best mitigates test set overfitting in hyperparameter search?
questions.choice_A: Reusing the test set to pick the best learning rate
questions.choice_B: Using a validation set or cross-validation to select hyperparameters and evaluating once on the untouched test set
questions.choice_C: Averaging validation and test scores during tuning
questions.choice_D: Tuning on a public leaderboard until performance saturates

questions.question: In a multi-benchmark comparison across 20 tasks, which correction is most appropriate if controlling the expected proportion of false discoveries is acceptable?
questions.choice_A: Bonferroni correction
questions.choice_B: Holm–Bonferroni correction
questions.choice_C: Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate control
questions.choice_D: No correction; report raw p-values

questions.question: Which element is essential for making experiments reproducible by external researchers?
questions.choice_A: Summarizing the main results verbally
questions.choice_B: Providing only final model checkpoints without metadata
questions.choice_C: Releasing code with exact dependency versions, seed initialization details, and environment specs (e.g., CUDA/cuDNN, drivers), ideally via containers
questions.choice_D: Publishing a high-level blog post

questions.question: When designing ablations for a new optimization trick that claims faster convergence, which design minimizes confounding?
questions.choice_A: Changing the optimizer and the learning rate schedule simultaneously
questions.choice_B: Keeping data, batch size, compute budget, and model identical, varying only the new trick, and matching wall-clock or FLOPs rather than epochs
questions.choice_C: Comparing at a single checkpoint chosen after seeing results
questions.choice_D: Evaluating on a subset of the data with altered class distribution

questions.question: Which runtime reporting practice best enables fair cross-hardware comparison in large-model training?
questions.choice_A: Reporting only wall-clock time without hardware specs
questions.choice_B: Reporting both wall-clock time and a hardware-agnostic proxy such as estimated training FLOPs, with explicit hardware and software configuration
questions.choice_C: Reporting the number of epochs without batch size details
questions.choice_D: Reporting tokens/sec from the very first iteration only

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Bayesian optimization over random search for hyperparameter tuning in expensive training runs?
questions.choice_A: It guarantees finding the global optimum
questions.choice_B: It eliminates the need for a validation set
questions.choice_C: It uses a surrogate model to guide sampling toward promising regions, improving sample efficiency
questions.choice_D: It is trivially parallelizable without trade-offs

questions.question: If model A and model B are evaluated per-example on the same test set producing correlated binary correctness outcomes, which test is most appropriate to assess whether their accuracies differ?
questions.choice_A: Unpaired t-test on accuracies
questions.choice_B: Wilcoxon rank-sum test on per-example correctness
questions.choice_C: Chi-squared test for independence ignoring pairing
questions.choice_D: McNemar's test on the disagreement contingency table

questions.question: Which practice best addresses the instability caused by seed variability in large model training?
questions.choice_A: Reporting a single run with the best result
questions.choice_B: Averaging two runs and omitting variability
questions.choice_C: Running multiple seeds, reporting mean and confidence intervals, and providing per-seed logs/checkpoints
questions.choice_D: Fixing the seed but changing the data order during training

questions.question: What is a common pitfall when using early stopping for hyperparameter selection?
questions.choice_A: Underreporting compute used
questions.choice_B: Biasing model selection toward configurations with faster initial gains, potentially missing better asymptotic performers
questions.choice_C: Overestimating memory usage
questions.choice_D: Violating the i.i.d. assumption of the test set

questions.question: Which reporting guideline most improves the transparency of benchmark comparisons?
questions.choice_A: Reporting only aggregate scores without task-level results
questions.choice_B: Plotting only the best seed and hiding others
questions.choice_C: Providing task-level metrics with uncertainty, exact data versions/splits, pre-processing steps, and links to evaluation scripts
questions.choice_D: Using custom private test sets without description

questions.question: You suspect that floating-point nondeterminism is causing rare evaluation discrepancies. Which procedure helps quantify the impact without retraining?
questions.choice_A: Re-running evaluation multiple times with deterministic kernels enabled and fixed seeds to estimate variance, and comparing to standard evaluation
questions.choice_B: Changing the dataset version and re-evaluating
questions.choice_C: Lowering the precision from float32 to bfloat16
questions.choice_D: Averaging predictions across models trained with different architectures

questions.question: For large-scale open releases, which practice best balances reproducibility and resource constraints?
questions.choice_A: Releasing only the final numbers to reduce storage
questions.choice_B: Open-sourcing code, configs, and eval scripts; releasing inference checkpoints; providing training traces/metrics and data manifests; and documenting known pitfalls and license constraints
questions.choice_C: Publishing raw proprietary data for transparency
questions.choice_D: Providing a single monolithic script without configuration files
